blurb: Charred-oak near-black with a copper pitched at the red end of the metal band — the colour of a cask hoop catching one lamp, not a sale banner. Rotating the brand off amber toward copper also walks the palette away from Beeline's black-and-yellow, which the owner's Espresso & Amber was structurally imitating.
risk: Copper and any credible red converge under deuteranopia (ΔE 6.6 fill / 8.9 ink versus the destructive), so delete must stay text-and-outline with «Удалить» carrying the meaning, never a filled red button.

blurb: The best accent in the set moved onto the most original surface anyone proposed — a greige faceplate rather than white paper, so the copper sits on stone instead of floating on a page. This is the daylight half of «Медь и обожжённый дуб», for the windscreen-at-noon case where a near-black screen turns into a mirror.
risk: A mid-tone ground spends contrast everywhere: it carries the least headroom of the light options, so the four inherited status colours need their darker light-theme siblings before this ships.

blurb: Warm rice-paper ground and antique brass — letterpress restraint, an engraved instrument plate rather than a promotion, with the ink kept brown-black so nothing on the page is truly grey. It is also the only one of the three that survives an Almaty windscreen at noon, where a near-black screen becomes a mirror.
risk: Brass fill clears only 3.15:1 on paper so the primary button leans on its dark engraved label and hairline for edge definition, and the four non-owner status colours need darker light-theme siblings before this ships.

blurb: A dark theme with no black anywhere in it — the ground is unglazed clay-brown, so the screen reads as a fired pot rather than a switched-off display, and the warm neutrals never go cold at the bottom of the ramp. The terracotta fill takes a cream label the way Hermès packaging does, and the amber status floats two full stops above it on a 3.6× luminance gap.
risk: The lifted brown ground spends contrast headroom everywhere: the accent fill clears the 3:1 affordance floor by only 0.14, so darkening the accent even slightly breaks it.

blurb: Lime-washed paper, warm the whole way down with no dead grey anywhere, holding a burnt sienna that reads as fired brick in daylight instead of a discount sticker. This is the sunlight palette — body ink at 16.3:1, every label above 5:1, and a copper button with a warm-white face that a 55-year-old can find outdoors without squinting.
risk: The oxblood owner_needed and the destructive red share a hue family and separate only by a 1.7× lightness step, so they must never wear the same shape — outlined pill with a glyph versus plain text.

blurb: A near-black char ground carrying a smoky tobacco-copper that behaves like worn saddle leather rather than a sale banner — deliberately the least saturated accent of the three (okC 0.10) so the amber status pill can outrank it without a fight. The accent-as-text lands at 5.98:1, bright enough to survive Almaty window glare, while the fill stays dark and matte with a cream label at 4.7:1.
risk: The most restrained accent in the set: a deep bronze fill sitting 3.4:1 above the surface can read as 'brown button' rather than 'the brand colour' to anyone expecting a vivid orange.

blurb: A warm near-black with almost no colour left in it, then one true orange at full chroma — the screen is brown-grey restraint until the button, which lands like a switch being thrown. Every orange fill carries a near-black label, so nothing goes white-hot and nothing halates on OLED.
risk: Its original #FF7A1F was ΔE 1.9 from Tailwind orange-500 and 3.2 from Dodo Pizza; this is re-cut to okC 0.155 / okH 53 to clear them. Still the hottest accent here — keep it under roughly a tenth of the screen or it reads as a sale banner rather than a tool.
